## 固定收益開盤主論述

美國與伊朗戰事再起，油價隨之上漲，市場擔心能源成本會讓通膨維持在足以促使聯準會升息的水準。8月31日，美國公債自5年期至長端全面走跌：10年期殖利率上升3.1個基點至4.751%，創2025年1月以來最高；30年期上升3.6個基點至5.243%，5年期上升2.1個基點至4.501%，2年期則微降0.2個基點至4.343%。

這種期限分布扭轉了主席Kevin Warsh在傑克森霍爾演說後殖利率曲線大幅趨平的部分走勢，但沒有消除市場對政策利率路徑上移的預期。2s10s曲線陡峭化3.3個基點至40.8個基點，2s30s擴大3.8個基點至90.0個基點。10年期實質殖利率上升2.8個基點至2.43%，幾乎解釋全部名目殖利率變動；損益兩平通膨率僅上升0.3個基點至2.321%。換言之，市場要求更高的通膨調整後報酬，而非大幅上調長期通膨補償。

直接觸媒是美伊在約一個月未直接交火後再度互襲。美軍攻擊荷莫茲海峽一座島嶼，伊朗隨後攻擊阿拉伯聯合大公國與約旦；美國總統Donald Trump表示美方將會回應，但未說明方式。WTI期貨於紐約收盤上漲3.55%至$86.36，再度引發市場疑慮：能源供應中斷可能加劇Warsh所稱尚未明顯降溫的通膨壓力。Brent期貨則回吐早盤漲幅，收跌0.81%至$88.59。地緣政治風險雖主導盤中利率走勢，兩大原油指標的收盤方向卻不一致。

Warsh的政策訊號仍是核心因素，因為投資人已將9月會議視為可能採取行動的會議。他演說後，貨幣市場賦予升息約60%的機率，Barclays與Société Générale經濟學家也改為預測今年將升息。週一的油價衝擊沒有再次推高政策敏感的2年期殖利率，卻使長天期債券未能得到地緣政治緊張時通常出現的支撐。投資人反而聚焦於能源壓力、就業韌性及聯準會是否落實鷹派訊號的不確定性，可能使政策利率與市場要求的實質報酬均維持高檔。

月底指數再平衡對長端的支撐也很有限。紐約時間下午4時，納入基準指數的10至30年期美國公債規模高於往常，但30年期殖利率仍然收高。再平衡前後短短一分鐘內，近244,000口12月10年期美債期貨成交，接近全日成交量的10%。現券交易同樣熱絡：FINRA記錄的美國公債面額成交量為$1.818兆，較前一交易日增加34.4%，其中名目附息債達$1.462兆；超過7年、但不超過10年的附息債交易量增加30.1%。

實質殖利率上升與地緣政治不確定性重現，也反映在風險資產上。S&P 500下跌0.58%，Nasdaq 100下跌0.62%，半導體指數重挫2.92%。美元指數上升0.26%；黃金期貨上漲0.44%至$4,498，8月全月漲幅達11.09%。VIX上升2.83%，但仍僅14.92，顯示這是幅度受控的重新定價，而非廣泛的市場失序。投資級債券部位下跌0.49%，主要高收益債基金約跌0.07%，新興市場債券部位則下跌0.38%。

美債賣壓只是全球緊縮動能的一環。印度成長優於預期，推高當地殖利率；德國通膨在歐洲央行9月會議前升溫；華盛頓施壓東京升息之際，日本10年期公債殖利率逼近3%。哥倫比亞新政府披露額外$110億融資需求，則形成較具本國特殊性的資金衝擊。企業信用方面，加州公用事業債券因野火責任法案走弱；CDK Global與UBS也正推動資本結構調整，但對債權人保障的影響截然不同。

## 油價與聯準會不確定性再度壓抑長天期美債

中東情勢最新升級，改變了投資人進入週一交易時所依據的能源市場背景。美國與伊朗約一個月來首次互相攻擊，使市場期待荷莫茲海峽航運恢復正常的希望受挫。即使生產商與航運業者藉由關閉識別訊號航行及船對船轉運因應，這場衝突仍已使波斯灣出口較戰前水準大幅減少。Goldman Sachs估計，近期波斯灣每日出口約1,500萬至1,600萬桶，仍比戰前少700萬至800萬桶，但已較3月低點增加500萬至600萬桶。

出口部分回升讓原油持續流通，卻未能恢復市場對供應中斷即將結束的信心。新一輪攻擊使實體航道、航運風險及通膨後果重新納入利率定價。10年期損益兩平通膨率僅上升0.3個基點，顯示市場沒有把單日戰事解讀為長期通膨大幅上升；實質殖利率上升2.8個基點則更具意義。在能源壓力可能迫使聯準會維持限制性政策、債券供給又沉重的環境下，投資人要求更高的債券持有補償。

10年期殖利率突破4.75%也具有額外意義，因為這項基準回到19個月未見的水準。5年期殖利率同樣升至2025年初以來最高，30年期則突破前一週高點。選擇權交易員尋求防範長債進一步下跌，其中約$650萬資金買進12月美國公債期貨賣權；其履約價相當於30年期殖利率從約5.25%升向5.7%。選擇權於11月20日到期，避險期間跨越下一次聯準會會議，並延伸至秋季融資日程。

企業發債是另一項可能推高長天期供給壓力的因素。9月歷來是債券發行旺月，今年發行量預料將超越過往9月紀錄。在投資人已評估現行殖利率能否充分補償財政風險、能源不確定性，以及聯準會減少提供詳細前瞻指引的情況下，這批供給將與美國財政部借款競逐資金。

財政部擴大長天期債券買回，仍可緩和部分壓力。該部表示，將把原訂買回的流通中10至30年期債券規模至少提高一倍；即使週一上漲，30年期殖利率仍低於8月稍早創下的多年高點。政策公布後，Brandywine Global降低對長天期美債的減碼幅度。財政部長Scott Bessent週一則主張，這項行動可能有助於美國公債8月表現優於其他主要主權債市。

相對表現部分支持Bessent的說法，但未平息對政策干預的爭議。美國10年期殖利率8月約上升2個基點，德國升幅超過10個基點，日本則上升15個基點。Bessent表示，其目標是減緩市場單向波動、讓焦點回到基本面，而不是決定殖利率方向。Stanley Druckenmiller等批評者則認為，政策制定者應讓債券市場自行發揮這項功能，不應提供裁量性支撐。

兩者的差別在於，買回可以改變長天期債券所在部位與交易流動性，卻不會消除政府整體融資需求。週一的賣壓顯示，即使財政部進場，長債仍會對油價、政策前景及相互競爭的供給作出反應。Bessent也延後原先承諾的財政整頓說明。他先前暗示可能在8月底左右公布，如今則表示，將在未來數週或數月與白宮預算主任Russ Vought討論一套方案。

在這項財政背景下，Warsh的政策反應函數仍是更大的不確定性來源。他表示，近期通膨數據雖有改善，卻不足以證明基礎通膨正以足夠速度明確趨近2%。聯準會6月與7月均維持利率不變，投資人仍懷疑其是否會在9月把鷹派言論化為升息行動。TD Securities仍以按兵不動為基本情境；ABN AMRO、Brandywine與DWS則警告，若通膨持續僵固，再次暫停升息可能重新引發公信力疑慮。

8月31日的曲線同時反映上述兩面。2年期殖利率沒有延續週五11.2個基點的升勢，顯示市場不願僅因油價上漲，就大幅加碼近期緊縮預期。較長天期殖利率則因能源衝擊、企業債供給及聯準會是否落實政策訊號的不確定性而上升，投資人要求額外補償。曲線因此單日陡峭化，但與一週前相比仍較平坦：2s10s一週仍收窄5.6個基點，2s30s收窄9.3個基點。

美元也呈現鷹派貨幣政策與干預式債務管理之間的張力。擴大債券買回計畫再度引發美國政策偏好弱勢美元的揣測，Bloomberg美元現貨指數繼7月下跌1.3%後，8月再跌0.9%；即使週五受Warsh言論提振，該指數週一仍下跌0.2%。以期貨計算的美元指數週一則收高0.26%。投資人因而區分財政部政策的整月影響，以及美國利率預期上升與地緣政治避險需求帶來的即時支撐。

## 印度、德國與日本強化全球緊縮動能

印度4至6月經濟較上年同期成長7.8%，高於7.3%的預測中位數及印度央行的7%預測。前一季成長率由7.8%上修至8.6%，為現行資料序列最高。結果降低市場對能源成本上升與供應中斷已使國內動能脫軌的疑慮，也強化印度央行今年稍後升息的預期。

成長動能分布廣泛。製造業成長由8.3%加速至9.2%，金融服務業由8.8%加速至12.1%。固定資本形成總額較上年同期增加11.9%，超過前一季5.8%增幅的兩倍；民間消費成長7.1%，也高於先前的6.8%。生產、服務、投資與家庭需求同步擴張，使這份數據對政策的意義高於僅由單一波動性產業推動的亮眼總體數字。

數據公布後，印度公債維持跌勢，指標10年期殖利率上升4個基點至6.95%。印度央行8月將政策利率維持在5.25%，但已表示若通膨升高，可能需要緊縮。Kotak Mahindra Bank首席經濟學家Upasna Bhardwaj預期，本財政年度下半年將升息50個基點，因為強勁成長與高通膨並存，通膨調整後利率也正在下降。

官方看法較為審慎。首席經濟顧問V. Anantha Nageswaran表示，通膨仍在印度央行2%至6%的容忍區間內，政策制定者將先觀察第二輪效應再採取行動。印度近90%的原油仰賴進口，因此特別容易受到荷莫茲海峽情勢影響。強勁的國內活動提高經濟吸收油價衝擊的能力，但也使央行更沒有理由容忍能源成本持續向其他物價傳導。印度央行下一次政策檢討定於10月5日至7日。

德國則提供更直接的通膨訊號。8月消費者物價較上年同期上升2.9%，高於7月的2.8%，並創4月以來最大增幅。雖然低於3.1%的預測中位數，通膨加速仍強化歐洲央行9月10日再度升息的理由。能源是主要推力，服務與食品通膨則有所降溫。

這種組合意味著，歐洲央行正面對尚未演變為國內通膨廣泛再加速的能源衝擊。管理委員會委員Martin Kocher表示，第二輪效應的證據仍不明確，應會在秋季變得更清楚；斯洛維尼亞央行總裁Primoz Dolenc則認為，9月升息的理由已經成立。歐洲央行存款利率目前為2.25%，被形容為既不刺激、也不抑制需求；官員已討論政策是否需要小幅進入限制性區間。

軍事支出與人工智慧投資支撐這個由21個成員組成的經濟體，成長表現優於預期。這份韌性為歐洲央行因應能源衝擊提供空間，但德國數據低於預期，也不宜據此假設將展開長期連續升息。近期決策的訊號日益明確，接下來的問題是能源成本是否會充分傳導至薪資與服務價格，以致明年仍需進一步升息。

日本債市的調整已走得更遠。週一，10年期日本公債殖利率一度觸及2.95%，為1996年以來最高，並在週二標售前逼近3%。升勢反映市場對日本央行升息的預期、財政供給疑慮，以及美國利率維持高檔時穩定日圓的困難。

Bessent在北卡羅來納州舉行的20國集團會議期間，與日本財務大臣片山皋月及日本央行總裁植田和男會晤，進一步加大政策壓力。NHK引述美國財政部國際事務次長Erin Browne報導，Bessent告訴日方官員，日本下一步應提高利率，並強調必須使公共財政走上可持續道路。這比他先前表示相信日本央行會採取正確行動更為明確。

這些言論把匯率政策、利率與財政公信力連結起來。美元兌日圓自美日聯合干預後首次突破160，週五收在160.09；至週一紐約午後回落至159.69，但日圓在干預期間取得的升幅已回吐逾半。此前一個月，日本投入創紀錄的¥15.4兆、即$964億；美國則未公布其較小規模的投入。

選擇權市場沒有呈現與現貨匯率相同的急迫感。日圓升值選擇權溢價較8月初極端水準約收窄三分之二，日本官員也持續強調匯率變動的速度與失序程度，而非固定價位。儘管如此，策略師仍指出，161及162至163區間可能提高干預風險。這使市場預期日本央行9月採取的行動，必須承擔更多扭轉日圓基礎利差劣勢的責任。

週二10年期公債標售將檢驗接近3%的殖利率能否吸引日本國內買盤。上一次標售的投標倍數為2.56，是2025年5月以來最低；上週2年期公債標售需求也偏弱。10年期標售結果將於東京時間下午12時35分公布。若需求疲弱，殖利率突破3%的壓力將升高；若投標較強，則顯示在日本央行9月17日至18日會議前，這波重新定價已開始吸引長期資金。

日本政府年金投資基金是潛在需求的核心，但尚未決定調整配置目標。GPIF管理約¥318兆資產，目前將25%配置於日本國內債券，因此每調整1個百分點便相當於逾¥3兆資產。第一生命經濟研究所的Koji Okuda認為，現行殖利率已足以讓GPIF考慮把目標提高至30%至35%，但仍須由GPIF評估不同經濟情境下的報酬與風險。

GPIF已透過例行再平衡增持日本債券。Nomura估計，該基金4至6月買進¥5.7兆日本債券，至少是2020財政年度以來最高的單季金額。正式提高配置目標則是規模大得多的行動：Okuda估計，若將日本國內債券比重提高至30%、同時減少外國債券，需要買進約¥16兆；若目標升至35%，買進規模將達¥32兆。

反對理由也相當充分。GPIF表示，目前投資環境與既有投資組合所假設的情況沒有重大差異；分析師並指出，名目殖利率上升部分源於薪資成長，不代表通膨調整後報酬已有決定性改善。提高日本國內債券比重，也可能迫使基金在其他部位承擔更多風險，才能達成長期報酬高於名目薪資成長率1.9個百分點的目標。目前而言，調整配置的可能性可在殖利率接近3%時提供需求，但投資人等待貨幣政策收緊之際，公債標售仍須依靠實際買盤順利消化。

## 哥倫比亞融資衝擊考驗新興市場韌性

哥倫比亞新政府在上週披露的財政惡化之外，又帶來迫切的借款衝擊。公共信貸主管Cesar Arias告訴造市商，政府計畫今年額外籌措約$110億，並透過債務交換管理2026年的融資需求。其中逾$30億預計來自外部借款，主要透過發債；國內市場則將籌集約25兆披索。

政府先前估計2027年財政赤字將達GDP的9.4%，引發的賣壓因這項宣布而延續。上週五披露赤字預測後，10年期本地公債殖利率上升逾30個基點，披索一度貶值2.1%。週一本地殖利率與交換利率再度上升，披索下跌0.9%，是當日表現最差的新興市場貨幣。

新資訊使市場焦點由赤字規模轉向市場能否提供足夠融資。BTG Pactual將借款計畫形容為重大的供給衝擊，預期曲線中段與長端將承受最大幅度的調整。接下來的標售將顯示政府是否必須提供更大的殖利率讓利，或接受較弱需求，尤其是在較長天期券種。

多邊機構借款可減少直接向債券投資人籌資的規模。財政部長Miguel Gómez預定在9月7日當週前往紐約與華盛頓，但已表示哥倫比亞並非尋求國際貨幣基金紓困。T. Rowe Price的Christopher Mejía認為，若政府落實財政整頓法案，並利用多邊機構及其他來源限制債券供給，擴大的借款需求仍可管理。因此，下一項信用考驗不再只是資訊透明度，而是能否實際執行調整方案。

這波重新定價發生在一段異常強勁的漲勢之後。高殖利率、強勢披索，以及市場對總統Abelardo de la Espriella當選的樂觀情緒，推動哥倫比亞本地債券今年以來報酬達29%，居新興市場同類資產之冠。累積漲幅為市場提供相當緩衝，但也說明財政起點惡化為何引發如此劇烈的反應。投資人如今必須依據立即增加的融資需求重估價值，而不能只依賴未來恢復財政規則的承諾。

整體新興市場表現仍較有韌性。截至週一，本幣新興市場債券今年上漲3.3%，已開發市場同類債券則下跌1.9%；即使美伊戰爭3月爆發時，新興市場一度下跌3.8%，相對優勢仍然存在。JPMorgan Asset Management、Invesco及Marlborough的基金經理人認為，部分韌性來自若干開發中經濟體更有紀律的通膨目標與財政政策，以及投資人對美元以外資產的需求。

美國公債殖利率與油價再度上升，直接挑戰這項資產配置。美國10年期殖利率若逼近5%，可能吸引資金回流美元資產；能源成本升高則會削弱原油進口國的財政與外部收支。週一主權債走勢凸顯同一資產類別內的差異：即使Moody’s調降評等，塞內加爾2033年到期美元債仍上漲0.4美分；哥倫比亞則因新的國內供給衝擊而遭到拋售。

智利投資人則審慎朝相反方向移動。在一項涵蓋24名分析師與交易員的調查中，17%受訪者願意在9月買進評等低至BBB的公司債，比例超過前一個月的三倍，並創3月以來最高。態度轉變之前，國會已通過總統José Antonio Kast經濟法案的核心內容，包括降低企業稅與減少監管。法案預計於9月上半月生效，預算辦公室則預測明年經濟成長3.7%。

財政取捨限制了增持較低品質信用債的理由。智利經濟在第1季萎縮0.3%後，第2季陷入停滯；改革預計將使政府收入至少連續5年減少。政府總債務正逼近GDP的45%，部分分析師認為這個水準將提高降評風險。因此，投資人是在期待投資復甦的前提下承擔更多企業信用風險，而主權資產負債表則吸收促成復甦的部分成本。

## 公用事業責任、CDK與UBS重新界定債權人保障

加州議員否決州長Gavin Newsom將野火成本移離上市公用事業公司的核心提案後，相關債券走弱。週一早盤，PG&E票息6.3%、2056年到期債券的利差擴大15個基點至138個基點；Edison International票息4%、2047年到期票據的利差則擴大10個基點至133個基點。

週六提出的法案將更新加州野火責任制度，卻不會阻止保險公司透過代位求償向公用事業公司追討損失。Newsom原本提議取消這條途徑，以降低公用事業公司資產負債表承受未來火災索賠的風險。Impax Asset Management的Tony Trzcinka表示，刪除這項內容對公用事業信用具有重大負面影響，即使評等遭調降也不令人意外。

議員擔心取消代位求償會促使保險公司提高家庭保費。他們提出的替代方案包括：禁止保險公司把對公用事業公司的債權出售給避險基金等投資人；在特別嚴重的火災後限制執行長獎金；加速賠付受災者；以及擴大防災計畫。這些規定可能改變債權持有人及受災者獲賠方式，卻不會消除公用事業公司的基礎責任。表決預計於週二舉行。

CDK Global則達成性質截然不同的債權人協議。Brookfield Business Partners與貸款人指導委員會同意一套負債管理架構，Brookfield將把約$6.75億自身持有的債務交換為順位較低的以債付息（PIK）債券。發起人持債降為次順位，可提高參與交易的擔保貸款人之相對順位；CDK則能以新增債務支付利息，從而保留現金。

作為交換，指導委員會的貸款人將以8%折價，把2029年到期的擔保債務換成延後兩年半到期的新債。若Brookfield在交易完成前持續於次級市場回購債務，可從這些債權人取得更大的本金折減。回購金額上限約為$12億，折價幅度最高可達13%。

這項架構透過順位、到期日與買入價格重新分配價值，並未減輕CDK的營運困境。公司近$40億、2029年到期的定期貸款，上週五價格為面額的52美分。CDK正面對獲利疲弱、高槓桿，以及2024年網路攻擊延續至今的影響。Moody’s在8月初以營收低迷、槓桿與再融資風險為由，將其評等下調兩級至Caa2。

指導委員會的合作協議禁止成員脫離團體，另行協商不同條件。CDK將尋求其餘貸款人同意，但不得給予他們優於委員會成員的待遇。這項保障降低參與者日後因他人取得更優惠交易而被降為較低順位的風險，發起人的債務交換也進一步提高其順位。不過，即使到期日延後，最終回收仍取決於公司能否在新債到期前穩定獲利。

UBS則取得一項暫時性的政治讓步，影響可能擴及整體其他第一類資本債券市場。瑞士國會上議院經濟與稅務委員會以10票贊成、2票反對及1票棄權，建議允許改革後的AT1證券滿足UBS新增資本要求的最高50%。瑞士政府要求約$200億額外資本，以免UBS海外子公司的虧損威脅其國內實體。

若一半要求可由可轉換債券滿足，UBS必須持有的普通股權益將減少，融資成本也可降低。UBS約占歐洲$2,860億AT1市場的7%，因此擬議中的重新設計不僅影響一家具重要地位的既有發行人，也會改變投資人對整個資產類別所要求的條件。

這項讓步的前提是AT1必須更早吸收損失。依委員會支持的方案，一旦UBS低於最低普通股權益要求，便須停止股利、股票回購及AT1票息，並削減員工獎金池。這些限制旨在讓相關工具於銀行持續經營的壓力階段便開始發揮作用，而不是直到進入處置程序才吸收損失。

決策尚未定案。財政部質疑AT1債務能否像普通股權益一樣可靠地吸收損失；下議院可能推翻部分讓步，社會民主黨也批評委員會的立場。下一步是上議院在9月14日至10月2日秋季會期表決，後續立法程序預計至少持續至2027年。

信用市場其他領域方面，亞洲資料中心貸款快速擴張，已開始碰到銀行集中度限制。2025年初以來，該產業貸款額接近$290億；2026年至今總額已達創紀錄的$150億，較去年同期增加27%。總部位於新加坡的DayOne Data Centers正洽談把既有融資額度提高至最高$70億，若完成，將成為亞洲規模最大的資料中心債務融資。

Barclays銀行家表示，隨著曝險累積，貸款機構的選擇日益嚴格，偏好成熟借款人或報酬較高的交易。部分機構正設法釋出承作空間或移轉風險：Crédit Agricole尋求出售一筆香港資料中心貸款的部分部位，Morgan Stanley則研究以重大風險移轉交易對沖曝險。

下一階段融資可能更倚重資產擔保證券與專案債券。美國光纖基礎設施及資料中心業者發行的資產擔保證券，去年增加86%至約$230億，為亞洲銀行把資本循環至長期市場提供參考模式。這種轉變可擴大投資人基礎，但也會把建設、使用率及科技風險移入證券，而其保障取決於專案現金流與擔保品。

Nvidia透過可轉換債券向台灣MediaTek投資$35億，顯示科技生態系內資本流動的規模。這是Nvidia在美國以外最大筆直接投資，目的是把其加速運算平台延伸至客製化系統。交易為半導體合作夥伴帶來策略資本；資料中心貸款數據則顯示，為部署相關技術所需實體容量提供融資的銀行，也同步承受壓力。

## 後續市場意義

美國第一批考驗於9月1日登場。S&P Global製造業指數終值將在紐約時間上午9時45分公布，市場預期為53.2，前值53.9。上午10時公布的ISM製造業指數預計為55.2，前值55.6；其中訂單、就業與價格分項將顯示，在能源成本重新推高投入價格壓力之際，工業需求是否仍然穩健。

7月職缺與營建支出同樣在上午10時公布。JOLTS職缺預計由735.9萬降至730萬，將在週五非農就業報告前更新勞動需求情況。營建支出預計在前月下降0.1%後持平，可用來觀察最直接受到長期利率高企影響的產業之一。

8月非農就業仍是對聯準會更重要的考驗。經濟學家預計，在7月意外減少後，就業人數將增加55,000人，失業率維持4.1%。若結果接近預測，將支持Warsh所稱就業大致穩定的判斷，使通膨繼續成為政策的主要限制；即使油價仍高，明顯較弱的勞動數據也會強化再次按兵不動的理由。

9月11日公布的消費者物價，將進一步判斷夏季較有利的通膨數據，是否已形成Warsh要求的明確趨勢。9月16日的聯準會決策，則會檢驗其傑克森霍爾標準究竟導向升息，或再次依數據暫停。若勞動或通膨明顯轉弱，暫停升息的含義將與證據沒有清楚改變時仍選擇暫停大不相同；後者可能使長天期債券重新承受公信力壓力。

日本10年期公債標售是眼前最重要的全球長天期事件。週二東京時間中午12時35分公布的結果，將顯示接近3%的殖利率能否在日本央行9月17日至18日會議前吸引退休基金、保險公司及其他國內買家。上次投標倍數僅2.56，加上上週2年期標售需求疲弱，形成偏低的需求比較基準。週四的30年期標售，則將另行檢驗超長天期債券面對財政政策與利率上升時的需求。

市場預期紐西蘭央行週三將官方現金利率調升25個基點至2.75%。受訪的21名經濟學家全數預期升息，交換市場反映的機率為95%。第2季通膨加速至4.1%，高於1%至3%的目標區間；但經濟上季可能萎縮，失業率也升至11年高點5.6%。政策聲明與總裁Anna Breman的記者會將顯示，10月是否可能再次升息，或央行可在利率朝接近3%的中性水準移動時暫緩行動。

歐洲央行9月10日決策將接續德國2.9%的通膨數據與更廣泛的歐元區資料。升息會使存款利率高於目前的中性水準；更關鍵的是政策指引，因其將決定能源衝擊是否需要在2027年進一步緊縮。若服務與薪資仍受控，將支持有限度調整；若傳導範圍擴大，則會強化採取限制性政策的理由。

加州週二的立法表決，將決定野火法案是否保留讓PG&E與Edison繼續面對保險公司索賠的條款。CDK必須讓其餘貸款人加入交換，且不得給予比指導委員會更優惠的待遇。UBS則將在9月14日至10月2日會期面對上議院表決，屆時議員將決定提前限制票息及股東分配，能否使AT1債務具備足夠可信度，以取代部分擬議中的普通股權益要求。

哥倫比亞公債標售將顯示，在國內市場籌措25兆披索需要提供多少讓利；Gómez於9月7日當週前往紐約與華盛頓會談，也將釐清外部債券與多邊融資所扮演的角色。DayOne最高$70億融資案的條件尚未確定，將檢驗當產業曝險逼近內部限額時，亞洲銀行能否再分銷一筆創紀錄的資料中心貸款。

overall_summary.headline: 油價衝擊推升實質殖利率，美國10年期公債殖利率升至19個月高點
overall_summary.session_narrative:
美國與伊朗戰事再起，能源風險重返美國公債市場。美軍攻擊荷莫茲海峽一座島嶼，伊朗攻擊阿拉伯聯合大公國與約旦，美國總統Donald Trump則表示美方將會回應。WTI上漲3.55%至$86.36，Brent卻下跌0.81%至$88.59，兩大原油指標收盤方向分歧。

美國10年期公債殖利率上升3.1個基點至4.751%，創19個月高點；30年期上升3.6個基點至5.243%。5年期升至4.501%，2年期則微降0.2個基點至4.343%，使2s10s陡峭化至40.8個基點，2s30s擴大至90.0個基點。10年期實質殖利率上升2.8個基點，幾乎解釋全部名目殖利率變動；損益兩平通膨率僅上升0.3個基點，顯示投資人要求更多通膨調整後補償，而非大幅上調長期通膨預期。

這波走勢扭轉了主席Kevin Warsh在傑克森霍爾演說後殖利率曲線趨平的部分幅度，但沒有消除政策利率路徑上移的預期。油價風險、聯準會9月是否升息的不確定性及潛在企業債供給，使長天期債券持續承壓；月底指數需求與財政部擴大債券買回，也未能阻止長端下跌。印度、德國與日本進一步增強全球緊縮動能，哥倫比亞額外$110億融資計畫則形成另一項新興市場資金衝擊。

## Opening Fixed-Income Thesis

Treasuries sold off from the 5-year sector through the long end on Aug. 31 as renewed fighting between the US and Iran lifted oil and reinforced the risk that energy costs will keep inflation high enough for the Federal Reserve to raise rates. The 10-year yield rose 3.1 basis points to 4.751%, its highest level since January 2025, while the 30-year added 3.6 basis points to 5.243%. The 5-year climbed 2.1 basis points to 4.501%, but the 2-year edged 0.2 basis point lower to 4.343%.

That distribution reversed part of the sharp flattening that followed Chair Kevin Warsh’s Jackson Hole speech without undoing the increase in the expected policy path. The 2s10s curve steepened 3.3 basis points to 40.8 basis points, and 2s30s widened 3.8 basis points to 90.0. At 10 years, the real yield rose 2.8 basis points to 2.43%, accounting for almost all the nominal move, while the breakeven increased just 0.3 basis point to 2.321%. The market therefore demanded a higher inflation-adjusted return rather than pricing a large additional rise in long-run inflation compensation.

The immediate catalyst was a new exchange of attacks after about a month without direct US-Iran strikes. American forces hit an island in the Strait of Hormuz, and Iran responded with attacks on the United Arab Emirates and Jordan. President Donald Trump said the US would respond, without specifying how. WTI futures gained 3.55% to $86.36 at the New York close, reviving concern that disrupted energy supply could reinforce the inflation pressure Warsh has said is not yet slowing meaningfully. Brent futures gave back an earlier advance and finished 0.81% lower at $88.59, leaving a divided close across the principal crude benchmarks even as geopolitical risk drove the intraday rates move.

Warsh’s policy signal remained central because investors were already treating the September meeting as live. Money markets assigned roughly a 60% probability to an increase after his speech, and economists at Barclays and Société Générale moved to forecasts that included higher rates this year. Monday’s oil shock did not push the policy-sensitive 2-year higher again, but it prevented longer maturities from receiving the usual support associated with geopolitical stress. Investors instead focused on the possibility that energy pressure, resilient employment and uncertain Fed follow-through would keep both policy rates and required real returns elevated.

The long end also received little help from month-end index rebalancing. A larger-than-usual amount of 10- to 30-year Treasury debt entered benchmarks at 4 p.m. in New York, yet 30-year yields remained higher. Nearly 244,000 December 10-year futures contracts changed hands during a single minute around the rebalance, almost 10% of the day’s volume. Cash-market activity was also heavy: FINRA recorded $1.818 trillion of Treasury par traded, 34.4% more than in the previous session, including $1.462 trillion of nominal coupons. Activity in coupons longer than 7 years and no more than 10 years rose 30.1%.

Risk assets reflected the combination of higher real yields and renewed geopolitical uncertainty. The S&P 500 fell 0.58%, the Nasdaq 100 declined 0.62% and the semiconductor index lost 2.92%. The Dollar Index rose 0.26%, while gold futures gained 0.44% to $4,498 and finished August 11.09% higher. The VIX increased 2.83% but remained at 14.92, indicating a contained repricing rather than broad market disorder. Investment-grade bond exposure fell 0.49%, while the main high-yield funds declined about 0.07%; emerging-market debt exposure lost 0.38%.

The US selloff was one part of a wider tightening impulse. Stronger-than-expected Indian growth lifted local yields, German inflation increased before the European Central Bank’s September meeting, and Japanese 10-year yields approached 3% as Washington pressed Tokyo to raise rates. Colombia faced a more idiosyncratic funding shock after its new government disclosed an additional $11 billion financing need. In corporate credit, California utility bonds weakened on wildfire-liability legislation, while CDK Global and UBS moved toward capital-structure changes with materially different implications for creditor protection.

## Oil and Fed Uncertainty Return Pressure to Long Treasuries

The latest Middle East escalation changed the energy backdrop that investors had carried into Monday. The US and Iran exchanged attacks for the first time in about a month, frustrating hopes that traffic through the Strait of Hormuz would normalize. The conflict has already reduced Gulf exports materially from prewar levels even as producers and shippers adapt through dark crossings and ship-to-ship transfers. Goldman Sachs estimated recent Gulf exports at roughly 15 million to 16 million barrels a day, still 7 million to 8 million below prewar levels but 5 million to 6 million above the March low.

That partial recovery has kept oil flowing without restoring confidence that the disruption is ending. The latest attacks brought the physical route, shipping risk and inflation consequences back into the rates calculation. The modest 0.3-basis-point increase in the 10-year breakeven showed that the market did not translate one session’s fighting into a large permanent inflation shock. The 2.8-basis-point rise in the real yield was more consequential: investors required greater compensation for holding duration in an environment where energy pressure may keep the Fed restrictive and where supply remains heavy.

The 10-year’s move above 4.75% carried additional significance because it returned the benchmark to a level not seen in 19 months. Five-year yields also reached their highest point since early 2025, and 30-year yields exceeded the previous week’s highs. Options traders sought protection against a further long-bond decline, including about $6.5 million spent on December Treasury-bond futures puts with a strike consistent with the 30-year yield rising toward 5.7% from around 5.25%. The options expire Nov. 20, extending the hedge beyond the next Fed meeting and into the autumn financing calendar.

Corporate issuance is another source of prospective duration pressure. September has historically been a large month for bond sales and is expected to exceed previous September totals. That supply will compete with Treasury borrowing at a time when investors are already assessing whether current yields sufficiently compensate for fiscal risk, energy uncertainty and a Fed that has become less willing to offer detailed forward guidance.

Treasury’s expansion of long-maturity buybacks still limits part of that pressure. The department has said it will at least double planned purchases of outstanding 10- to 30-year securities, and the 30-year yield remained below the multiyear highs reached earlier in August despite Monday’s increase. Brandywine Global reduced its underweight in long Treasuries after the announcement, while Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent argued Monday that the action may have helped US government bonds outperform other major sovereign markets during August.

The relative comparison supports part of Bessent’s claim without settling the controversy over intervention. The US 10-year yield was up about 2 basis points for August, compared with increases of more than 10 basis points in Germany and 15 basis points in Japan. Bessent said his objective was to slow one-way market behavior and keep attention on fundamentals, rather than dictate the direction of yields. Stanley Druckenmiller and other critics have argued that policymakers should allow the bond market to perform that function without discretionary support.

The distinction matters because buybacks alter the location and tradability of duration without eliminating the government’s aggregate financing requirement. Monday’s selloff showed that long bonds remain responsive to oil, the policy outlook and competing supply even with Treasury in the market. Bessent also pushed a promised fiscal-consolidation presentation farther into the future, saying he and White House budget director Russ Vought would discuss a package in the coming weeks or months after previously suggesting an announcement could arrive around the end of August.

Warsh’s reaction function remains the larger source of uncertainty at the front of that fiscal backdrop. He has said recent inflation readings were better but did not demonstrate that underlying inflation was moving clearly toward 2% at sufficient speed. Investors nevertheless question whether the Fed will follow the rhetoric with a September increase after holding rates steady in June and July. TD Securities retained a hold as its base case, while ABN AMRO, Brandywine and DWS warned that another pause could revive credibility concerns if inflation remains sticky.

The Aug. 31 curve reflected both sides of that argument. The 2-year yield did not extend Friday’s 11.2-basis-point rise, suggesting the market was not prepared to add materially to near-term tightening expectations solely because oil increased. Farther out, yields climbed as the energy shock, corporate supply and uncertainty over Fed execution demanded additional compensation. That produced a daily steepening even though the curve remained flatter than a week earlier: 2s10s was still 5.6 basis points narrower over the week, and 2s30s was 9.3 basis points narrower.

The dollar also captured the tension between hawkish monetary policy and interventionist debt management. The Bloomberg Dollar Spot Index fell 0.9% in August after declining 1.3% in July, as the enlarged buyback program renewed speculation that US policy favored a weaker currency. It declined another 0.2% Monday by that measure, despite Friday’s boost from Warsh. The futures-based Dollar Index, by contrast, ended Monday 0.26% higher. Investors are therefore distinguishing between the month-long effect of Treasury policy and the immediate support from higher US rate expectations and geopolitical demand.

## India, Germany and Japan Add to the Global Tightening Impulse

India’s economy expanded 7.8% from a year earlier in the April-June quarter, exceeding the 7.3% median forecast and the Reserve Bank of India’s 7% projection. Growth in the previous quarter was revised to 8.6% from 7.8%, the strongest reading in the current data series. The result reduced concern that higher energy costs and supply disruption had already derailed domestic momentum and strengthened expectations that the RBI could raise rates later this year.

The composition was broad. Manufacturing growth accelerated to 9.2% from 8.3%, and financial services expanded 12.1% after 8.8%. Gross fixed-capital formation increased 11.9% from a year earlier, more than double the previous quarter’s 5.8% pace, while private consumption grew 7.1% compared with 6.8%. That combination of production, services, investment and household demand gave the release greater policy relevance than a headline driven by one volatile sector.

Indian government bonds retained their losses after the data. The benchmark 10-year yield rose 4 basis points to 6.95%. The RBI kept its policy rate at 5.25% in August but has indicated that tightening may be needed if inflation builds. Upasna Bhardwaj, chief economist at Kotak Mahindra Bank, expects 50 basis points of increases in the second half of the fiscal year because robust growth is coinciding with elevated inflation and falling inflation-adjusted interest rates.

The official assessment was more cautious. Chief Economic Adviser V. Anantha Nageswaran described inflation as contained within the RBI’s 2%-to-6% tolerance band and said policymakers were watching for second-round effects before acting. India remains particularly exposed to the Strait of Hormuz because it imports nearly 90% of its crude. Strong domestic activity improves the economy’s ability to absorb an oil shock, but it also gives the central bank less reason to tolerate a sustained energy pass-through. The RBI’s next policy review runs from Oct. 5 to Oct. 7.

Germany supplied a more direct inflation signal. Consumer prices rose 2.9% from a year earlier in August, up from 2.8% and the strongest rate since April. The result was below the 3.1% median estimate, but the acceleration reinforced the case for another European Central Bank increase on Sept. 10. Energy was the main driver, while services and food inflation eased.

The mix leaves the ECB confronting an energy shock that has not yet become a broad new increase in domestic inflation. Governing Council member Martin Kocher said evidence of second-round effects remained unclear and should become more visible during the autumn. Slovenian Governor Primoz Dolenc has argued that the case for a September increase is already present. The ECB’s deposit rate is 2.25%, a level described as neither stimulating nor restricting demand, and officials have discussed whether policy must move modestly into restrictive territory.

Growth has held up better than expected as military expenditure and artificial-intelligence investment support the 21-member economy. That resilience gives the ECB room to respond to the energy shock, but the below-consensus German reading also cautions against assuming a prolonged sequence of increases. The immediate decision is increasingly well signaled; the question is whether energy costs spread into wages and services strongly enough to require further moves next year.

Japan’s adjustment is more advanced in the bond market. The 10-year government-bond yield touched 2.95% Monday, its highest since 1996 and close to the 3% level ahead of Tuesday’s auction. The rise reflects expectations for a Bank of Japan increase, concern about fiscal supply and the difficulty of stabilizing the yen while US rates remain high.

Bessent intensified the policy pressure during meetings with Japanese Finance Minister Satsuki Katayama and BOJ Governor Kazuo Ueda at the Group of 20 gathering in North Carolina. According to NHK, citing Treasury Under Secretary for International Affairs Erin Browne, Bessent told the Japanese officials that the country’s next step should be higher interest rates and emphasized the need to put public finances on a sustainable path. That was more explicit than his earlier statement that he expected the BOJ to do the right thing.

The comments connected currency policy, interest rates and fiscal credibility. The yen had breached 160 per dollar for the first time since the joint US-Japan intervention and ended Friday at 160.09. It recovered to 159.69 by Monday afternoon in New York but had surrendered more than half the appreciation achieved during the intervention campaign. Japan spent a record ¥15.4 trillion, or $96.4 billion, over the preceding month, while the US has not disclosed its smaller contribution.

Options markets did not show the same urgency as the spot level. The premium for yen appreciation was roughly two-thirds narrower than at its early-August extreme, and Japanese officials continued to emphasize the speed and disorderliness of currency moves rather than a fixed threshold. Strategists nevertheless identified 161 and the 162-to-163 region as levels where intervention risk could increase. That leaves the BOJ’s expected September action carrying more of the burden of changing the yen’s underlying rate disadvantage.

Tuesday’s 10-year auction will test whether yields near 3% have become attractive enough to bring in domestic buyers. The previous sale’s bid-to-cover ratio was 2.56, the weakest since May 2025, and a 2-year auction last week also drew poor demand. The 10-year results are due at 12:35 p.m. Tokyo time. A weak sale would increase pressure on the yield to move through 3%, while stronger demand would show that the repricing is beginning to recruit long-term capital before the BOJ’s Sept. 17-18 meeting.

The Government Pension Investment Fund is central to that prospective demand, although it has made no decision to change its target. GPIF manages about ¥318 trillion and currently allocates 25% to domestic bonds, making a 1-percentage-point shift equivalent to more than ¥3 trillion of assets. Koji Okuda of Daiichi Life Research Institute argued that yields now justify considering an increase in the target to 30%-35%, subject to GPIF’s assessment of returns and risks across economic scenarios.

GPIF has already added domestic debt through ordinary rebalancing. Nomura estimated that it purchased ¥5.7 trillion of Japanese bonds in the April-June quarter, the largest quarterly amount since at least fiscal 2020. Raising the formal target would be a much larger step: Okuda estimated that increasing domestic bonds to 30% while reducing foreign debt would require about ¥16 trillion of yen purchases, rising to ¥32 trillion at a 35% target.

There are substantial objections. GPIF said the investment environment was not materially different from that assumed in its existing portfolio, and analysts noted that higher nominal yields partly reflect wage growth rather than a decisive improvement in inflation-adjusted returns. Increasing domestic bonds could also require greater risk-taking elsewhere to meet the fund’s long-term objective of exceeding nominal wage growth by 1.9 percentage points. For now, the prospect of rebalancing offers demand near 3%; it does not remove the need for auctions to clear while investors await tighter monetary policy.

## Colombia’s Funding Shock Tests Emerging-Market Resilience

Colombia’s incoming government added an immediate borrowing shock to the fiscal deterioration disclosed last week. Public credit director Cesar Arias told market makers that the administration planned to raise about $11 billion of additional financing this year and conduct debt swaps to manage its 2026 needs. More than $3 billion is expected to come from external borrowing, mainly bond sales, while approximately 25 trillion pesos would be raised in the local market.

The announcement extended a selloff that began after the government estimated a 2027 fiscal deficit equal to 9.4% of GDP. The Friday disclosure drove the 10-year local government-bond yield more than 30 basis points higher and weakened the peso by as much as 2.1%. Local yields and swap rates rose again Monday, while the peso fell 0.9%, the weakest performance among emerging-market currencies that day.

The new information shifted the issue from the size of the deficit to the market’s capacity to finance it. BTG Pactual described the borrowing plan as a significant supply shock and expects the belly and long end of the curve to bear the largest adjustment. Upcoming auctions will reveal whether the government must offer larger yield concessions or accept weaker demand, particularly in longer maturities.

Multilateral borrowing could reduce the volume placed directly with bond investors. Finance Minister Miguel Gómez is due to travel to New York and Washington during the week of Sept. 7, though he has said Colombia is not seeking an International Monetary Fund rescue. T. Rowe Price’s Christopher Mejía judged the larger borrowing manageable if the government implements its fiscal-consolidation law and uses multilaterals and other sources to limit bond supply. That condition makes execution of the adjustment program, rather than transparency alone, the next credit test.

The repricing follows an exceptional rally. Colombian local bonds have returned 29% this year, the best performance among emerging-market peers, supported by high yields, a strong peso and optimism surrounding President Abelardo de la Espriella’s election. Those gains leave the market with a substantial cushion, but they also explain why the deterioration in the fiscal starting point produced a sharp response. Investors must now reassess valuations against an immediate financing increase rather than a distant promise to restore the fiscal rule.

Broader emerging-market performance remained more resilient. Local-currency emerging-market bonds gained 3.3% this year through Monday, while developed-market peers lost 1.9%, even after a 3.8% emerging-market decline when the US-Iran war began in March. Fund managers at JPMorgan Asset Management, Invesco and Marlborough attributed part of that relative strength to more disciplined inflation targeting and fiscal policy in several developing economies, as well as demand for assets outside the dollar.

The renewed rise in Treasury yields and oil is a direct challenge to that allocation. A 10-year US yield approaching 5% could pull capital back toward dollar assets, while higher energy costs weaken the fiscal and external balances of importing countries. Monday’s sovereign moves illustrated the distinction within the asset class: Senegal’s 2033 dollar bond rose 0.4 cent despite a Moody’s downgrade, while Colombia sold off on a fresh domestic supply shock.

Chile showed investors cautiously moving in the other direction. In a survey of 24 analysts and traders, 17% were willing to buy corporate bonds rated as low as BBB for September, more than triple the previous month’s share and the highest since March. The shift followed congressional approval of the core of President José Antonio Kast’s economic bill, including lower corporate taxes and reduced regulation. The legislation is expected to be enacted in the first half of September, and the budget office forecasts 3.7% growth next year.

The fiscal trade-off limits the case for lower-quality credit. Chile’s economy stagnated in Q2 after contracting 0.3% in Q1, and the reform is expected to reduce government revenue for at least 5 years. Gross debt is approaching 45% of GDP, a level some analysts associate with greater downgrade risk. Investors are therefore accepting more corporate risk on expectations of an investment revival while the sovereign absorbs part of the cost of producing it.

## Utility Liability, CDK and UBS Redefine Creditor Protection

California utility bonds weakened after lawmakers rejected a central part of Governor Gavin Newsom’s proposal to shift wildfire costs away from publicly traded utilities. The spread on PG&E’s 6.3% bonds due in 2056 widened 15 basis points to 138 basis points early Monday, while Edison International’s 4% notes due in 2047 widened 10 basis points to 133 basis points.

The bill introduced Saturday would update the state’s wildfire framework but would not prevent insurers from pursuing utilities through subrogation. Newsom had proposed eliminating that route, which would have reduced the exposure of utility balance sheets to future fire claims. Tony Trzcinka of Impax Asset Management described the omission as materially negative for utility credit and said rating downgrades would not be surprising.

Lawmakers were concerned that removing subrogation would lead insurers to raise premiums for households. Their alternative would prohibit insurers from selling claims against utilities to investors such as hedge funds, restrict chief executive bonuses after especially severe fires, accelerate payments to survivors and expand prevention programs. Those provisions may change who holds claims and how victims are paid, but they do not remove the utilities’ underlying liability. A vote is expected Tuesday.

CDK Global reached a very different kind of creditor agreement. Brookfield Business Partners and a lender steering committee agreed on a liability-management framework under which Brookfield would exchange about $675 million of its debt for lower-ranking payment-in-kind paper. Subordinating the sponsor’s holdings would improve the relative position of participating secured lenders while allowing CDK to conserve cash by paying interest with additional debt.

In return, steering-committee lenders would exchange secured obligations due in 2029 for debt maturing 2½ years later at an 8% discount. Brookfield could obtain a larger haircut from those creditors if it continues repurchasing debt in the secondary market before the transaction closes. The repurchase amount is capped at about $1.2 billion, and the discount could reach 13%.

The structure redistributes value through priority, maturity and purchase price rather than reducing CDK’s operating challenges. Its nearly $4 billion term loan due in 2029 traded at 52 cents on Friday. The company is contending with weak earnings, high leverage and the continuing consequences of a 2024 cyberattack. Moody’s lowered its rating by 2 notches to Caa2 in early August, citing muted revenue, leverage and refinancing risk.

The steering committee’s cooperation agreement prevents members from leaving the group to negotiate separate terms. CDK will seek agreement from the remaining lenders, but their treatment cannot be better than that offered to committee members. That protection reduces the risk that participants will later be subordinated by a superior deal, while the sponsor’s exchange gives them additional priority. The maturity extension still leaves recovery dependent on whether the company can stabilize earnings before the new debt comes due.

UBS won an interim political concession with implications for the broader Additional Tier 1 market. The Economic Affairs and Taxation Committee of Switzerland’s upper house voted 10-2, with one abstention, to recommend that reformed AT1 securities be allowed to satisfy as much as 50% of the bank’s proposed additional capital requirement. The government has sought roughly $20 billion of extra capital to prevent losses in UBS’s foreign subsidiaries from threatening its domestic entity.

Allowing half the requirement to be met with convertible debt would reduce the amount of common equity UBS must hold and lower its funding cost. UBS accounts for about 7% of Europe’s $286 billion AT1 market, so the proposed redesign would affect a major existing issuer as well as the terms investors demand across the asset class.

The concession depends on making AT1s absorb losses earlier. Under the committee-backed approach, a fall below UBS’s minimum common-equity requirement would stop dividends, share repurchases and AT1 coupons while reducing the employee bonus pool. Those restrictions are intended to make the instruments function during a going-concern stress period rather than only at the point of resolution.

The decision is not final. The Finance Ministry has questioned whether AT1 debt can absorb losses as reliably as common equity, the lower house may reverse some of the concession, and the Social Democrats criticized the committee’s stance. The next step is a vote in the upper house during its Sept. 14-Oct. 2 autumn session, followed by a legislative process expected to continue at least into 2027.

Elsewhere in credit, the rapid expansion of Asian data-center lending is beginning to encounter bank concentration limits. Loans to the sector have reached nearly $29 billion since the start of 2025. The total for 2026 is already a record $15 billion, 27% more than in the comparable period last year, and Singapore-based DayOne Data Centers is discussing an increase in an existing facility to as much as $7 billion. That would be Asia’s largest data-center debt financing.

Barclays bankers said lenders are becoming more selective as exposure accumulates, favoring established borrowers or transactions that offer higher returns. Some institutions are trying to free capacity or transfer risk: Crédit Agricole sought to sell part of a Hong Kong data-center loan, while Morgan Stanley explored a significant-risk-transfer transaction to hedge exposure.

The next phase of financing is likely to rely more heavily on asset-backed securities and project bonds. US sales of asset-backed securities by fiber-infrastructure and data-center owners rose 86% last year to about $23 billion, offering a template for recycling Asian bank capital into long-term markets. The shift would broaden the investor base but also move construction, utilization and technology risk into securities whose protection depends on project cash flows and collateral.

Nvidia’s $3.5 billion investment in Taiwan’s MediaTek through convertible bonds illustrates the scale of capital moving through the technology ecosystem. It is Nvidia’s largest direct investment outside the US and is intended to extend its accelerated-computing platform into customized systems. The transaction brings strategic capital to a semiconductor partner, while the data-center lending figures show the simultaneous pressure on banks financing the physical capacity required to deploy that technology.

## Forward Market Significance

The first US tests arrive Sept. 1. The final S&P Global manufacturing index is due at 9:45 a.m. New York time, with consensus at 53.2 after 53.9 previously. At 10 a.m., the ISM manufacturing index is expected at 55.2 after 55.6. Its orders, employment and prices components will show whether industrial demand remains firm while energy costs renew pressure on input prices.

July job openings and construction spending are due at the same time. JOLTS vacancies are expected at 7.3 million after 7.359 million, updating labor demand before Friday’s payroll report. Construction spending is expected to be unchanged after a 0.1% decline, providing a read on one of the sectors most directly exposed to elevated long-term rates.

August payrolls remain the larger Fed test. Economists expect employment to increase by 55,000 after an unexpected July decline, with unemployment holding at 4.1%. A result near that forecast would support Warsh’s judgment that employment is broadly steady and leave inflation as the principal constraint on policy. A materially weaker labor reading would strengthen the case for another hold even if oil remains elevated.

Consumer prices on Sept. 11 will then determine whether the favorable summer inflation readings have become the clearer trend Warsh said he requires. The Sept. 16 Fed decision will test whether his Jackson Hole standard leads to an increase or another data-dependent pause. A hold accompanied by weaker employment or inflation would differ materially from a hold without a clear change in the evidence, which could return credibility pressure to longer maturities.

Japan’s 10-year auction is the immediate global-duration event. Results at 12:35 p.m. Tokyo time Tuesday will show whether a yield near 3% attracts pension funds, insurers and other domestic buyers before the BOJ meets on Sept. 17-18. The previous bid-to-cover ratio of 2.56 and last week’s weak 2-year sale set a low demand baseline. Thursday’s 30-year auction will provide a separate test of super-long exposure to fiscal policy and higher rates.

New Zealand’s central bank is expected to raise its Official Cash Rate by 25 basis points to 2.75% on Wednesday. All 21 economists surveyed expect the move, and swaps assign a 95% probability to it. Inflation accelerated to 4.1% in Q2, above the 1%-to-3% target band, but the economy may have contracted last quarter and unemployment has risen to an 11-year high of 5.6%. The policy statement and Governor Anna Breman’s news conference will indicate whether another increase in October is likely or whether the bank can wait as it moves toward a neutral rate near 3%.

The ECB’s Sept. 10 decision will follow Germany’s 2.9% inflation reading and the broader euro-area data. An increase would move the deposit rate above its current neutral setting; guidance will matter more for determining whether the energy shock requires additional tightening in 2027. Evidence that services and wages remain contained would support a limited adjustment, while broader pass-through would strengthen the case for restrictive policy.

California’s Tuesday legislative vote will determine whether the wildfire bill preserves the provisions that left PG&E and Edison exposed to insurer claims. CDK must bring remaining lenders into its exchange without granting better treatment than the steering committee received. UBS faces the upper-house vote during the Sept. 14-Oct. 2 session, where lawmakers will decide whether earlier coupon and distribution restrictions make AT1 debt credible enough to replace part of the proposed common-equity requirement.

Colombia’s auctions will show how much concession is needed to place 25 trillion pesos locally, while Gómez’s meetings in New York and Washington during the week of Sept. 7 will clarify the role of external bonds and multilateral financing. For DayOne, the unresolved terms of a facility as large as $7 billion will test whether Asian banks can distribute another record data-center loan as sector exposure approaches internal limits.

section_summaries.section_title: Oil and Fed Uncertainty Return Pressure to Long Treasuries
section_summaries.summary: Fresh US-Iran strikes returned Hormuz disruption to the rates calculation even though Gulf exports had partly recovered. The 10-year moved above 4.75% for the first time in 19 months as real yields, rather than breakevens, drove the increase. Options hedges, expected September corporate issuance and uncertainty over Fed follow-through added duration pressure; expanded Treasury buybacks limited but did not remove it, and the promised fiscal-consolidation presentation slipped to the coming weeks or months.

section_summaries.section_title: India, Germany and Japan Add to the Global Tightening Impulse
section_summaries.summary: India's 7.8% growth beat forecasts, lifted its 10-year yield to 6.95% and strengthened expectations for RBI tightening despite official caution on inflation spillovers. German inflation rose to 2.9%, reinforcing the case for a Sept. 10 ECB increase while leaving further moves dependent on broader pass-through. Japan's 10-year yield touched 2.95% as fiscal supply, BOJ expectations and a weak yen converged; pressure from Washington raised the policy stakes, but auction demand and any GPIF allocation shift remain unresolved.

section_summaries.section_title: Colombia’s Funding Shock Tests Emerging-Market Resilience
section_summaries.summary: Colombia's new government plans about $11 billion of additional financing, including roughly 25 trillion pesos locally and more than $3 billion externally, after disclosing a 2027 deficit of 9.4% of GDP. The announcement shifted the concern from fiscal deterioration to market capacity, extending losses in local bonds and the peso after a 29% year-to-date rally. Broader EM debt remained resilient, but near-5% US yields and higher oil challenge that allocation; Chilean investors showed greater appetite for BBB credit even as tax reform raises sovereign trade-offs.

section_summaries.section_title: Utility Liability, CDK and UBS Redefine Creditor Protection
section_summaries.summary: California utility bonds weakened after lawmakers kept insurers' right to pursue utilities for wildfire claims, leaving PG&E and Edison exposed ahead of Tuesday's vote. CDK's exchange would subordinate $675 million of sponsor debt and improve participating lenders' priority, but recovery still depends on operating improvement. A Swiss committee backed using redesigned AT1 debt for as much as 50% of UBS's extra capital requirement, with earlier coupon and distribution restrictions. Asian data-center lending is reaching bank concentration limits, encouraging a shift toward asset-backed securities and project bonds.

US manufacturing data, JOLTS and construction spending on Sept. 1 lead into August payrolls, Sept. 11 CPI and the Sept. 16 Fed decision, with weak labor favoring a hold and persistent inflation keeping tightening credible. Japanese auctions will test demand near a 3% 10-year yield before the BOJ meets. The RBNZ is expected to raise rates, while ECB guidance will show whether Germany's energy-led inflation requires more than one move. California, CDK, UBS, Colombia and DayOne also face near-term votes, financing or creditor-execution tests.

overall_summary.headline: Oil shock lifts the 10-year Treasury yield to a 19-month high as real yields rise
overall_summary.session_narrative:
Renewed US-Iran fighting put energy risk back into the Treasury market. American forces struck an island in the Strait of Hormuz, Iran attacked the United Arab Emirates and Jordan, and President Donald Trump said the US would respond. WTI rose 3.55% to $86.36, although Brent fell 0.81% to $88.59, leaving a divided crude close.

The 10-year Treasury yield rose 3.1 basis points to 4.751%, its highest level in 19 months, and the 30-year added 3.6 basis points to 5.243%. The 5-year climbed to 4.501%, while the 2-year edged 0.2 basis point lower to 4.343%, steepening 2s10s to 40.8 basis points and 2s30s to 90.0. A 2.8-basis-point rise in the 10-year real yield accounted for almost all of the nominal move, while the breakeven increased just 0.3 basis point, indicating demand for more inflation-adjusted compensation rather than a large additional rise in long-run inflation expectations.

The move reversed part of the flattening after Chair Kevin Warsh's Jackson Hole speech without erasing the higher expected policy path. Oil risk, uncertainty over whether the Fed will raise rates in September and prospective corporate issuance kept pressure on duration, while month-end index demand and expanded Treasury buybacks failed to prevent the long-end selloff. India, Germany and Japan added to the global tightening impulse, and Colombia's additional $11 billion financing plan created a separate emerging-market funding shock.
